default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-1098.title: Same-minute drift persistence
E-1098.hypothesis: Intraday returns show time-of-day periodicity: a clock slot whose forward return was consistently one sign over the last 20 sessions (t-stat) keeps attracting the same-side flow (recurring institutional and hedging orders); trade the historical sign when the t-stat first exceeds the threshold.

E-1099.title: Clock-anchor level cross
E-1099.hypothesis: The price at a fixed clock time (10:00, 11:00, 12:00) is an anchor many traders reference as the morning/midday reference; after the price stays on one side for a while, the first close across it shows the other side taking control; follow it.

E-1100.title: Nested inside-bar chain break
E-1100.hypothesis: A chain of successively nested bars is a deeper compression than one inside bar: resting stops pile up beyond the mother bar's edges and a close beyond the last bar releases them.

E-1101.title: US-open box edge break
E-1101.hypothesis: Orders around the US cash open and data releases arrive in the 15 minutes after 10:30/11:00/11:30; the box of those minutes marks where foreign flow was absorbed, and a close beyond its edge in the following hours shows that flow winning; follow.

E-1102.title: Session-extreme count pressure
E-1102.hypothesis: When most of the last bars each print a new session high (or low), buyers (sellers) are being chased repeatedly by late participants and stops; the persistent pressure keeps going, so follow the first time the count reaches the threshold.

E-1104.title: Four-EMA ribbon onset
E-1104.hypothesis: When four exponential averages with doubling spans fall into strict order, trends of every horizon agree and trend-following funds add; follow the first bar the ordering completes.

E-1105.title: Elder-ray pullback in a rising EMA
E-1105.hypothesis: In a trending EMA, a bar whose low dips under the EMA but where the bear power is already improving and the close is up shows sellers losing force against the trend; buy it (mirror for sells).

E-1106.title: Ease-of-movement zero cross
E-1106.hypothesis: Ease of movement relates price change to volume per unit range: sustained positive values mean price advances with little resistance; a zero cross to positive means liquidity on the offer thinned out; follow.

E-1107.title: Awesome-oscillator saucer
E-1107.hypothesis: Inside an up-momentum regime (fast median mean above slow), two falling oscillator bars followed by a rising bar mark a pause where dip buyers re-enter; the saucer resumes the trend (mirror for sells).
